title: Scaling Molecular Dynamics with ab initio Accuracy to 149 Nanoseconds per Day
problem: Neural network-based molecular dynamics packages like DeePMD-kit achieve only 4.7 nanoseconds per day on the Fugaku supercomputer, which is insufficient for simulating physical phenomena requiring millisecond to microsecond timescale observations. Inter-node communication becomes a critical bottleneck when scaling to thousands of nodes.
motivation: Simulating chemical reactions, bond breaking, and phase transitions with ab initio accuracy requires efficient molecular dynamics implementations to make millisecond-scale studies computationally tractable within reasonable wall-clock times.
method: The authors implement a node-based parallelization scheme that reduces inter-node communication by 81% through optimized data decomposition. They accelerate compute-intensive kernels using SVE-GEMM (optimized matrix multiplication for Fugaku's A64FX CPUs) and mixed-precision arithmetic to reduce bandwidth and increase throughput. Intra-node load balancing is applied to distribute work evenly across processing units within each node.
key_novelty: Node-based parallelization scheme that reduces communication overhead by 81%, enabling efficient scaling of neural network molecular dynamics to tens of thousands of nodes.
contributions: Node-based parallelization scheme reducing inter-node communication by 81%
SVE-GEMM kernel optimization and mixed-precision implementation
Intra-node load balancing mechanism for improved resource utilization
31.7x performance improvement achieving 149 nanoseconds per day on 12,000 Fugaku nodes
limitations: Numerical accuracy implications of mixed precision and potential accumulated errors in long-time molecular dynamics simulations are not discussed.
primary_theme: Large-scale molecular dynamics acceleration on supercomputers
